questions.question: Yash travels 204 km at 68 km/hr, the next 424 km at 53 km/hr and the next 366 km at 61 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Corrected to two decimal places)
questions.solution:

Speed 1 (S₁) = 68 km/hr

Distance 2 (D₂) = 424 km

Speed 2 (S₂) = 53 km/hr

Speed 3 (S₃) = 61 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Total Distance = D₁ + D₂ + D₃

Total Time = (D₁ / S₁) + (D₂ / S₂) + (D₃ / S₃)

**Calculations:**

Total Distance = 204 + 424 + 366

⇒ Total Distance = 994 km

Total Time = (204 / 68) + (424 / 53) + (366 / 61)

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 8 + 6

⇒ Total Time = 17 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 994 / 17

⇒ Average Speed = 58.47 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A boat takes 75 minutes to go 62.3 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 3 : 2. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 67.6 km upstream and 35.8 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance traveled upstream = 62.3 km

Time taken upstream = 75 minutes = 75/60 = 1.25 hours

Speed ratio of boat in still water to stream = 3:2

Distance to be traveled upstream = 67.6 km

Distance to be traveled downstream = 35.8 km

Calculation:

Let the speed of the boat in still water be 3x and the speed of the stream be 2x.

Effective speed upstream = Speed of boat - Speed of stream = (3x - 2x) = x

Effective speed downstream = Speed of boat + Speed of stream = (3x + 2x) = 5x

Speed upstream = Distance / Time = 62.3 / 1.25

⇒ x = 49.84 km/h

Effective speed downstream = 5x = 5 × 49.84 = 249.2 km/h

Time taken upstream = Distance / Speed = 67.6 / x

⇒ Time upstream = 67.6 / 49.84 = 1.356 hours

Time taken downstream = Distance / Speed = 35.8 / 249.2

⇒ Time downstream = 35.8 / 249.2 = 0.144 hours

Total time = Time upstream + Time downstream

⇒ Total time = 1.356 + 0.144 = 1.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A 120 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 9 km/hr (in same direction) in 18 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 230 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 27 km/hr?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train 1 = 120 m

Speed of man = 9 km/hr

Time to overtake man = 18 s

Length of train 2 = 230 m

Speed of train 2 = 27 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed of train 1 w.r.t man = 120 ÷ 18 = 6.67 m/s

Man speed in m/s = 9 × 1000 ÷ 3600 = 2.5 m/s

⇒ Speed of train 1 = 6.67 + 2.5 = 9.17 m/s

Train 1 speed in km/hr = 9.17 × 18 ÷ 5 = 33 km/hr

Relative speed of train 1 & train 2 (opposite) = 33 + 27 = 60 km/hr

In m/s = 60 × 1000 ÷ 3600 = 16.67 m/s

Total distance to cross = 120 + 230 = 350 m

⇒ Time = 350 ÷ 16.67 = 21 s

**∴ The correct answer is 21 seconds.**

questions.question: A boat takes 27 minutes to go 40.6 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 8 : 7. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 77.7 km upstream and 52.5 km downstream?

2. Calculate total time:

Time upstream = Distance ÷ Speed = 77.7 ÷ x = 77.7 ÷ 90.2 = 0.862 hours

Time downstream = Distance ÷ Speed = 52.5 ÷ (15x) = 52.5 ÷ (15 × 90.2)

⇒ Time downstream = 52.5 ÷ 1353 = 0.0388 hours

Total time = Time upstream + Time downstream = 0.862 + 0.0388 = 0.9 hours

⇒ Total travel time without stoppages = 6 hours

Total travel time with stoppages = dfrac{528}{24}

⇒ Total travel time with stoppages = 22 hours

Total time for stoppages = Total travel time with stoppages - Total travel time without stoppages

⇒ Total time for stoppages = 22 - 6

⇒ Total time for stoppages = 16 hours

questions.question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 12.6 km/hr. The other one walks at 27 km/hr. The train takes 12.5 and 14 seconds, respectively, to overtake them. What is the speed of the train if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of person A = 12.6 km/hr

Speed of person B = 27 km/hr

Time taken to overtake A = 12.5 sec

Time taken to overtake B = 14 sec

**Formula used:**

Distance = Relative speed × Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

Let length of train = D meters

Speed of train = x km/hr

Relative speed w.r.t A = (x - 12.6) km/hr = (x - 12.6) × 5/18 m/s

D = (x - 12.6) × 5/18 × 12.5

Relative speed w.r.t B = (x - 27) km/hr = (x - 27) × 5/18 m/s

D = (x - 27) × 5/18 × 14

Equating both:

(x - 12.6) × 12.5 = (x - 27) × 14

⇒ 12.5x - 157.5 = 14x - 378

⇒ 220.5 = 1.5x

⇒ x = 220.5 ÷ 1.5 = 147 km/hr

**∴ Speed of the train is 147 km/hr.**

questions.question: A 250 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 7 km/hr (in same direction) in 50 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 280 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 28 km/hr?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train = 250 m

Speed of man = 7 km/hr

Overtaking time = 50 sec

Length of second train = 280 m

Speed of second train = 28 km/hr (opposite direction)

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Difference (same direction), Sum (opposite direction)

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed (in m/s) = km/hr × 5/18

**Calculation:**

Let speed of train = x km/hr

Relative speed with man = (x - 7) km/hr

⇒ (x - 7) × 5/18 = 250 / 50

⇒ (x - 7) × 5/18 = 5

⇒ x - 7 = 18

⇒ x = 25 km/hr

Speed of train = 25 km/hr

Now, relative speed with second train (opposite direction) = (25 + 28) = 53 km/hr

⇒ 53 × 5/18 = 265/18 m/s

Total length to cross = 250 + 280 = 530 m

Time = 530 ÷ (265/18)

⇒ Time = 530 × 18 / 265

⇒ Time = 36 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is Option (1).**

Speed of person 1 = 12.6 km/hr

Speed of person 2 = 30.6 km/hr

Time to overtake person 1 = 19.8 sec

Time to overtake person 2 = 25.8 sec

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Speed of train - Speed of person

Distance = Relative speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let speed of train = x km/hr

⇒ Relative speed with person 1 = (x - 12.6) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ Distance = (x - 12.6) × 5/18 × 19.8

⇒ Relative speed with person 2 = (x - 30.6) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ Distance = (x - 30.6) × 5/18 × 25.8

Since both distances are equal:

(x - 12.6) × 5/18 × 19.8 = (x - 30.6) × 5/18 × 25.8

⇒ (x - 12.6) × 19.8 = (x - 30.6) × 25.8

⇒ 19.8x - 249.48 = 25.8x - 789.48

⇒ 789.48 - 249.48 = 25.8x - 19.8x

⇒ 540 = 6x

⇒ x = 90 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is Option (2).**

Upstream speed = Boat speed - Stream speed

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Time downstream = 52.8 ÷ 12 = 4.4 hrs

Time upstream = 52.8 ÷ 2 = 26.4 hrs

Total time = 4.4 + 26.4 = 30.8 hrs

**∴ Total time taken is 30.8 hours.**

questions.question: A boat takes 76 minutes to go 32.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 9 : 8. How much approximate total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 44.9 km upstream and 57.8 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial upstream distance = 32.2 km

Initial upstream time = 76 minutes

Ratio of speed of boat (B) to speed of stream (S) = 9 : 8

**Formula Used:**

Speed = dfrac{{Distance}}{{Time}}

Upstream Speed = B - S

Downstream Speed = B + S

**Calculations:**

Initial upstream time in hours = dfrac{76}{60} hours

⇒ Initial upstream speed = dfrac{32.2}{(76)/(60)} = dfrac{32.2 times 60}{76} = 25.42 km/hr

Let the speed of boat (B) be 9x and speed of stream (S) be 8x.

⇒ Upstream Speed = B - S = 9x - 8x = x

So, x = 25.42 km/hr

⇒ Downstream Speed = B + S = 9x + 8x = 17x

⇒ Downstream Speed = 17 × 25.42 = 432.14 km/hr

Time for final upstream journey = dfrac{{Final upstream distance}}{{Upstream Speed}} = dfrac{44.9}{25.42}

⇒ Time for final upstream journey ≈ 1.77 hours

Time for final downstream journey = dfrac{{Final downstream distance}}{{Downstream Speed}} = dfrac{57.8}{432.14}

⇒ Time for final downstream journey ≈ 0.13 hours

Total time = Time upstream + Time downstream

⇒ Total time = 1.77 + 0.13 = 1.90 hours

**∴ The total approximate time is 1.90 hours.**

questions.question: Namita travels a certain distance at a speed of 88 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 16 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 33 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Namita travels a certain distance (D) at 88 km/hr.

She travels double the earlier distance (2D) at 16 km/hr.

Average speed for the entire journey = 33 km/hr.

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculations:**

Total distance = D + 2D + (D + 2D) = 6D

Time for first journey = t₁ = D / 88

Time for second journey = t₂ = 2D / 16

Time for return journey = t₃ = (D + 2D) / S = 3D / S

Total time = tTₒₜₐₗ = t₁ + t₂ + t₃

⇒ tTₒₜₐₗ = (D / 88) + (2D / 16) + (3D / S)

Average speed = 33 = Total distance / Total time

⇒ 33 = 6D / [(D / 88) + (2D / 16) + (3D / S)]

⇒ [(D / 88) + (2D / 16) + (3D / S)] = 6D / 33

⇒ [(D / 88) + (2D / 16) + (3D / S)] = D / 5.5

⇒ (1 / 88) + (2 / 16) + (3 / S) = 1 / 5.5

⇒ (1 / 88) + (1 / 8) + (3 / S) = 2 / 11

⇒ (1 / 88) + (11 / 88) + (3 / S) = 16 / 88

⇒ 12 / 88 + (3 / S) = 16 / 88

⇒ (3 / S) = (16 / 88) - (12 / 88)

⇒ (3 / S) = 4 / 88

⇒ S = (3 × 88) / 4

⇒ S = 66

**∴ The correct answer is option (1): 66 km/hr.**

questions.question: A train P going at the speed of 78 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 120 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 62 km/hr, in 4.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to cross completely train R of length 245 m, going at 81 km/hr in the opposite direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of P = 78 km/hr

Speed of Q = 62 km/hr, Length of Q = 120 m

Time to pass Q = 4.5 minutes = 270 s

Speed of R = 81 km/hr, Length of R = 245 m

**Formula used:**

Relative speed (same dir) = vP - vQ

Relative speed (opp dir) = vP + vR

km/hr to m/s: × 1000 ÷ 3600 = × 5 ÷ 18

Distance = Relative speed (m/s) × Time (s)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative speed (m/s)

**Calculations:**

⇒ vP - vQ = 78 - 62 = 16 km/hr

⇒ 16 km/hr in m/s = 16 × 5 ÷ 18 = (80 ÷ 18) = 40 ÷ 9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered while passing Q = (40 ÷ 9) × 270 = 40 × 30 = 1200 m

⇒ Length of P = 1200 - 120 = 1080 m

⇒ Relative speed with R (opposite) = 78 + 81 = 159 km/hr

⇒ 159 km/hr in m/s = 159 × 5 ÷ 18 = 795 ÷ 18 = 265 ÷ 6 m/s

⇒ Total distance to cross R = 1080 + 245 = 1325 m

⇒ Time = 1325 ÷ (265 ÷ 6) = 1325 × 6 ÷ 265 = 5 × 6 = 30 s

**∴ Time taken = 30 seconds.**

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = 14 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Amita travels a certain distance at a speed of 84 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 28 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 24 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Amita travels a distance at speed of 84km/h 

He travels double the distance at 28 km/h 

Average speed for entire journey is 24 km/h 

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled /Total time taken 

Calculation:

Let the distance travelled be x at speed of 84km/h

Now, time = x/84 h 

So, when distance gets doubled i.e. 2x at speed of 28 km/h 

Time = 2x/28= x/14 h 

Total time taken for going = (x/84 + x/14) = x/12 h

Now, average speed for the entire journey i.e. 3x + 3x = 6x is 24 km/h 

Time of complete journey = 6x/24 = x/4 h 

So, time of returning journey = ( x/4 - x/12) = x/6 h and distance = 3x

So, average speed of the returning journey = 3x/(x/6) = 18 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A train is 591 m and it crosses a platform in 1.7 minutes running at the speed of 36 km/hr. Find the difference between the length of the train and the platform.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train = 591 m

Time to cross platform = 1.7 min = 102 s

Speed of train = 36 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Length of platform = Distance - Length of train

Difference = |Length of train - Length of platform|

**Calculation:**

Speed in m/s = 36 times (5)/(18) = 10 m/s

Distance = 10 × 102 = 1020 m

Length of platform = 1020 - 591

⇒ Length of platform = 429 m

Difference = |591 - 429| = 162 m

**∴ The difference between the length of the train and the platform is 162 m.**
